patreon.title: Initialize: preparing a place for Git history
patreon.post:
Imagine a volunteer club newsletter folder containing a draft, photos, and notes. Initializing that folder prepares a local Git repository. Git creates the information it needs to support tracking changes and storing recorded history, usually in a hidden .git directory.

The key distinction: an initialized repository can have zero commits. Your existing files are not automatically staged or committed, and initialization does not upload them.

Takeaway: initialization prepares the history shelf; a deliberately recorded commit begins the history.

What did you assume initialization would do when you first encountered Git?

Sources: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-init https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Getting-a-Git-Repository

Narration uses the synthetic Friendly Instructor profile locally in VoiceStudio/VoxCPM2. Music is an original procedural local composition.
